source.topicTitle: Bean seed germination in a classroom tray

spans.excerpt: A bean seed contains a young plant inside a protective seed coat. In a classroom tray, a seed placed on damp cotton can take up water. A seed left on dry cotton does not take up enough water to begin germinating. Taking up water starts the changes that allow the young plant to grow.

After the seed takes up water, its seed coat splits. A small root appears first and grows downward. The root takes in water from the damp cotton. A shoot appears later and grows upward. These observations let a learner tell the early stages apart without guessing from the size of the seed alone.

The shoot needs light to make food once green leaves develop. A tray beside a bright window gives the leaves light. A tray kept in a dark cupboard does not give the leaves light for this process. Water helps the seed begin germinating, while light matters later when the leaves make food.
